# NavSentinel North-Star Internal Audit — Synthesis

*Source: 13 analysis agents over 9 subsystems + 4 cross-cutting hunts, adversarially verified against `main` (post-#195 batch, v0.4.0). Findings merged where semantically duplicate; verdict-corrections applied. File paths are absolute-within-repo (`extension/src/...`).*

---

## 1. Executive Assessment

**Goal 1 — Zero-FP Smart Mode: ~70% there, with three structural holes.** The scoring core (`scoring.ts`, `nrs.ts`) is principled and the same-org suppression in `domain_groups.ts` already fixed the headline unity3d.com FP. Measured FP is 0.72% on Tranco top-200 — close, but above the 0.1% target and, more importantly, the harness never exercises the flows the product vision explicitly names. The verified root causes are not random noise but **three coherent gaps**: (a) Smart Mode gates at *mode* level, not *signal* level (`capture_isolated.ts:1681` runs full scoring then prompts whenever `nrs < blockThreshold`), so OAuth callbacks, SSO/IdP redirects, 3DS payment hops, and cross-site `_blank` SSO links still surface prompts that should be silent (confirmed: capture-pipeline *Smart-Mode-gates-at-mode-level*, fp-hunter *cross-site `_blank` SSO*, *3DS redirect chains*, credential-guard *SSO/IdP gateways*); (b) the `intent_mismatch_under_interactive` +35 composite has no container-aware heuristic (confirmed FP driver); (c) there is **no top-sites trust prior and no session/familiarity suppression** — a global top-100k site that trips a heuristic is almost always a FP, but the codebase has no tier to lean on. Adaptive scoring exists but `computeAdjustment()` only shifts a per-domain threshold and is fed by a thin outcome log. Net: silent on the easy cases, predictably noisy on exactly the high-interaction flows (SSO, OAuth, payments, SPAs) the vision targets.

**Goal 2 — Friend-Advisor UX: ~30% there. Building blocks exist; the product does not.** `explanations.ts` maps ~41–49 reason codes to plain English, `debug_overlay.ts` renders the full CDS/NRS/factor breakdown, and `ui_toast.ts`/`credential_modal.ts` are solid accessible surfaces. But every load-bearing piece of the advisor experience is missing: there is **no user-facing decision journal** (EventLog and PromptOutcome are two unlinked streams shown in separate options panes — confirmed ux-advisor *CRITICAL: No persistent decision journal*, architecture-hunter *No Decision Journal*); **silent allows — the majority of normal browsing — emit zero events** (confirmed ux-advisor, advisor-hunter, feedback-hunter — three independent agents); explanations are wired into toasts but **not** into the options event log or popup chips (they render raw codes); the prompt toast shows only a one-line top reason, not "why"; and the adaptive adjustment that is silently tuning the user's thresholds is never surfaced. The verbose `debug` mode is real and user-togglable but framed as developer-only and not enabled by default. A user cannot answer "why did NavSentinel allow/block/prompt this, and when?" after the fact.

**Goal 3 — Live Feedback Capture: ~40% there. Infrastructure is robust; the payload is too thin to tune on.** The append/serialize/retry/reset-barrier plumbing (`storage.ts`) is production-grade, every prompt surface calls `appendPromptOutcome`, an export path exists, and adaptive scoring already reads the corpus. The fatal limitation: `PromptOutcomeEntry` records only `{domain, destDomain, type, score, outcome, reasons?}`, and on the navigation path even `reasons` is dropped (credential path does capture it — an inconsistency, confirmed across scoring-core, capture-pipeline, telemetry-feedback, feedback-hunter, advisor-hunter, architecture-hunter — six agents converge here). The full feature vector (NRS factor breakdown, CDS score, DOM/ElementHint context, adaptive adjustment applied, threshold used, nav context, redirect chain, gesture timing) is computed and sits in `lastDebug` but is discarded before storage. Consequence: **you cannot re-score or retrain offline from what is captured today.** There is also no "this was wrong" mislabel affordance, no silent-allow ground-truth signal, and no event↔outcome linkage. The corpus is good for behavior tracking, useless for supervised tuning.

**Goal 4 — Architecture Leverage: clear-eyed about the limits, with escape hatches scoped but blocked.** The audit confirms the real MV3 ceilings: no pre-commit blocking (reactive rollback shows a visible flash — though note the verified correction that proactive JS-API patching in `main_guard.ts` *is* the primary defense, so the "flash" is a top-frame-commit fallback, not the whole story); CSP header blindness (`csp_analyzer.ts` meta-tag only, #179); cross-origin iframe/subframe inspection gaps; per-frame domain-profile races under `all_frames` (#181); bridge has no post-verification liveness check; and a bridge session-replay/re-pin weakness (#186). The Firefox manifest and `browser.*` shim (FF-01) are merged but unwired — FF-02→04 is blocked on the **AI-4 tooling decision (OPEN)**, and Firefox's retained blocking `webRequest` is the single biggest unlock the codebase is leaving on the table. A native-messaging companion (the user's "antivirus-like" idea) is acknowledged as the highest-ceiling escape hatch but **not yet designed**. Visual-sim is plumbing-complete but inert (placeholder hashes, blocked on **AI-5, OPEN**), and the bloom filter is build-time-only with no runtime refresh (30–90 day staleness — confirmed critical). The architecture is honestly self-aware; the leverage is unrealized pending two human decisions.

> **OPEN human-owned items gating this work (must be surfaced): AI-3** (fate of `fix/jsb-stale-todos-and-tests`), **AI-4** (Firefox build tooling — blocks the entire architecture/platform program), **AI-5** (sanctioned brand screenshots — blocks visual-sim). AI-1/AI-2 resolved 2026-06-05.

## 2. Top 10 Priorities (ranked by product-impact-per-effort)

| # | Priority | Effort | Dependencies |
|---|----------|--------|--------------|
| 1 | **Signal-level Smart-Mode gating (suppress benign-context prompts)** | M | None (unblocks FP program) |
| 2 | **Enrich the capture record — widen `PromptOutcomeEntry` to a full feature vector** | S–M | None (unblocks tuning + journal) |
| 3 | **Top-sites trust-tier prior (build-time CrUX/Tranco tier) + threshold = f(tier)** | M | None |
| 4 | **User-facing Decision Journal (incl. silent allows) + wire `explainReasonCode` into all UI** | M–L | #2 (richer records make the journal worth reading) |
| 5 | **`intent_mismatch_under_interactive` container-aware heuristic** | S | None |
| 6 | **Bloom filter runtime refresh + staleness tracking** | M | Native companion (best) *or* signed-CDN fetch (interim) |
| 7 | **AI-4 decision → Firefox build (FF-02→04) → blocking `webRequest` escape hatch** | L (human gate first) | AI-4 (OPEN) |
| 8 | **"This was wrong" mislabel affordance on every intervention surface** | S | #2 |
| 9 | **Apply the (already-computed) adaptive adjustment to the live threshold + show it** | S | None |
| 10 | **Native-messaging companion — design spike + scoping** | M (design) / XL (build) | Product decision |

**1. Signal-level Smart-Mode gating.** *What:* In `capture_isolated.ts` (the `isLegitBlankAnchor`/decision path ~1681–1714), suppress prompts when context is provably benign: OAuth callback with `oauthRedirectMismatch===false` or known-IdP opener; same-registrable-org via `areSameOrganization`; user-activation-active short-gesture clicks with no CDS risk; recognized 3DS/payment-processor hops. *Why:* directly attacks the #1 vision goal — the verified FPs are concentrated here, not in random heuristics. *Supports:* capture-pipeline *Smart Mode gates at mode level*; fp-hunter *cross-site `_blank` SSO*, *3DS redirect chains*; credential-guard *SSO/corporate IdP*. *Deps:* none.

**2. Enrich the capture record.** *What:* Add optional fields to `PromptOutcomeEntry` (`storage.ts:55-64`): `reasonCodes[]`, `nrsFactors[]`, `cds`, `navAnomalyScore`, `adaptiveAdj`, `thresholdUsed`, serialized `ElementHint` context. Populate at every `appendPromptOutcome`/`appendOutcomeSafely` site (nav path *and* credential path — fix the inconsistency where nav drops `reasons`). *Why:* unblocks offline re-scoring/retraining (goal 3) AND makes the journal explainable (goal 2) — one cheap change serves two goals. *Supports:* scoring-core *No rich context telemetry* (critical); capture-pipeline *Solo click-time decision path lacks unified context* (critical); telemetry-feedback *Lightweight prompt outcome schema*; feedback-hunter *NRS factor breakdown discarded*; architecture-hunter *No Decision Journal*; advisor-hunter *Prompt outcomes lack context*. *Deps:* none. Note the verified nuance: `reasonCodes` already exists in scope and the optional `reasons` field already exists — much of this is wiring, not schema invention.

**3. Top-sites trust-tier prior.** *What:* Bundle a build-time CrUX/Tranco top-1M tier (same local-first pattern as PSL/bloom) and scale intervention threshold by tier (allowlisted→silent; top-tier+no-bad-signal→silent unless high-confidence attack; seen-before-benign→relaxed; unknown→normal; known-bad→strict). *Why:* the single highest-ROI structural FP lever — most heuristic trips on global-top sites are FPs by definition. *Supports:* fp-hunter *No adaptive thresholds for corporate domain patterns*, *user-activation +5 insufficient*; handoff §4 Goal-1 "biggest missing FP lever." *Deps:* none.

**4. User-facing Decision Journal + UI explanation wiring.** *What:* New options pane (best home: **Chrome Side Panel API**, MV3-native, non-interruptive) merging EventLog + PromptOutcome by domain+time proximity into a reverse-chron timeline with factor breakdown, threshold, and `explainReasonCode()` output; **emit a `nav_silent_allow` event** so silent decisions appear; wire `explainReasonCode` into the options event log and popup chips (currently raw codes). *Why:* this *is* the friend-advisor goal; warning-science says the journal is the non-interruptive channel that satisfies "advisor" without warning fatigue. *Supports:* ux-advisor *No persistent decision journal* (critical), *Silent decisions never explained* (high), *Reason codes never shown in UI*; advisor-hunter *Silent allow emits zero events* (critical), *Reason explanations exist but never shown*; sw-state *No verbose/decision-journal mode*; fp-hunter *No verbose audit mode*; test-harness *Decision journal missing*. *Deps:* #2.

**5. `intent_mismatch_under_interactive` container heuristic.** *What:* In `scoring.ts:128-137`, don't flag when the top element is container-like (`nav`, `div[role=navigation]`) without action intent; log the DOM relationship. *Why:* confirmed driver of the only measured Tranco FP; small, contained, high-confidence. *Supports:* scoring-core *intent_mismatch drives unity3d.com FP* (confirmed). *Deps:* none.

**6. Bloom filter runtime refresh.** *What:* Add a timestamp header to the `.bin` format, a scheduled (weekly) refresh from a signed source, staleness tracking in `chrome.storage.local`, and age-graceful degradation. *Why:* confirmed critical — users run 30–90 days stale against hourly-updating threat feeds; silently erodes TP. *Supports:* reputation-content *Bloom filter staleness* (critical). *Deps:* native companion is the clean structural fix; signed-CDN fetch is the MV3-native interim.

**7. AI-4 → Firefox blocking `webRequest`.** *What:* Make the AI-4 tooling call, implement FF-02→04, exploit Firefox's retained blocking `webRequest` for true pre-commit blocking Chrome MV3 cannot do. *Why:* eliminates the Chrome rollback flash on the platform that allows it; product differentiation. *Supports:* capture-pipeline *Firefox build disables main-world guard*; architecture-hunter *Firefox port stacked/blocked*, *Chrome MV3 cannot block before commit*; sw-state *Firefox session fallback not auto-cleared* (FF-03). *Deps:* **AI-4 (OPEN, human).**

**8. Mislabel affordance.** *What:* One-tap "this was wrong" on every intervention surface → flips a `wasWrong`/label field in the corpus → discounts FP outcomes in adaptive scoring. *Why:* cheap, single-user-friendly, turns the corpus into labeled training data and closes the FP feedback loop. *Supports:* feedback-hunter *No retroactive feedback affordance* (high); telemetry-feedback *Corpus not labeled for supervised tuning*; ux-advisor *No guidance on what to do with false positives*. *Deps:* #2.

**9. Apply + surface adaptive adjustment.** *What:* `decision_threshold = BASE + adaptiveAdj` (the value is computed and logged but the threshold stays hard-coded per the verified scoring-core finding); show "Threshold 70 → 75 (trusted)" in popup/journal. *Why:* makes the existing learning actually reduce FPs and makes it explainable. *Supports:* scoring-core *Adaptive adjustment sound but never applied*; advisor-hunter *Adaptive adjustments computed but never displayed* (high). *Deps:* none. (Verify the exact application path — the not-verified scoring-core item should be confirmed against `getNrsBlockThreshold`, which the advisor-hunter finding suggests *does* apply it; reconcile before implementing.)

**10. Native-companion design spike.** *What:* Scope a Go/Rust `nativeMessaging` helper for the structural fixes no extension can do (DNS inspection, persistent state, heavy ML, CSP-header capture, download scanning). *Why:* highest-ceiling escape hatch; takes the project from "extension" to "security companion." *Supports:* architecture-hunter (CSP blindness, no liveness, MV3 limits); reputation-content (bloom refresh, CSP headers); scoring-core *subframe inspection*. *Deps:* product decision; recommend AGAINST a browser fork (sober ROI, per handoff §4).

## 3. FP-Elimination Program

A coherent five-step plan from the `fp-source` findings (merged across scoring-core, capture-pipeline, credential-guard, main-world-guards, sw-state, fp-hunter):

**Step 0 — Instrument before tuning.** Land priority #2 (rich capture) and add a Smart-Mode-silence CI gate (`prompts-per-100-benign-pages ≈ 0`) that exercises the *named* vision flows (SSO multi-step + credential submit, OAuth redirect chains, 3DS, SPA route churn) — today `measure-fp.mjs` only does homepage + 3 link clicks (confirmed test-harness *Smart Mode Silence goal has no dedicated CI gate*, critical). Without measurement isolating which factor/context caused each FP, all tuning is guesswork.

**Step 1 — Trust-tier prior (priority #3).** Establishes the structural baseline: a top-sites tier + per-tier thresholds. This alone removes most heuristic trips on global-top sites.

**Step 2 — Benign-context signal gating (priority #1).** Suppress the verified FP clusters at signal level:
- OAuth/SSO/IdP: don't penalize cross-site action to known IdPs (okta, auth0, accounts.google, login.microsoftonline) — credential-guard *SSO/corporate IdP gateways* (high).
- 3DS/payment hops — fp-hunter *3DS payment redirect chains* (confirmed).
- Marketing redirectors — expand `TRACKING_PREFIX_ALLOWLIST` (Twitter/Slack/Instagram/SendGrid/Pipedrive) — sw-state *Redirect-chain allowlist not comprehensive*; fp-hunter *redirect chain not aware of marketing patterns*.
- Session-aware `_blank` suppression — fp-hunter *Insufficient suppression of cross-site `_blank` SSO* (after 2+ allows in session, suppress new-tab + cross-site).

**Step 3 — Fix specific scorers.**
- `intent_mismatch_under_interactive` container heuristic (priority #5) — the one measured Tranco FP.
- Split shared redirect allowance into per-kind buckets (form-submit vs location) — main-world-guards *Form-submit allowance shared* (confirmed: legit multi-step checkout exhausts the 2-redirect budget).
- PushState domain-like-path whitelist for semver/service segments — main-world-guards *PushState FP on SPAs* (confirmed).
- `detectLegitModalBackdrop`: recognize CSS-class modals (`modal`/`dialog`/`overlay`) and large legit overlays (video/cookie/accessibility), not just `role=dialog`/`aria-modal` — scoring-core *isLegitModalBackdrop limited*, *Viewport coverage cliff* (note the verified inversion: the ≥0.35 gate currently *prevents* attribute checking on 25–35% modals).
- JS-behavior allowlist integration: skip cross-origin exfil signals to allowlisted/payment-processor origins — visual-js-p4 *JS behavior monitor has no allowlist integration* (confirmed; the allowlist module exists but isn't passed to the monitor config).
- Cookie-consent suppression in ClickFix clipboard+overlay — fp-hunter *clipboard-copy buttons adjacent to overlays* (lower than claimed: scoring already needs command/instruction text, but explicit cookie-consent pattern would close the edge).

**Step 4 — Engagement/familiarity suppression + apply adaptive adjustment (priority #9).** Leverage `domain_profile.ts` visit history to relax thresholds on habitual sites; apply the computed `adaptiveAdj` to the live threshold. Re-run the corpus replay (step 0 gate) to measure FP/TP delta before shipping each change.

*Lower-confidence opacity/z-index/composite-escalation/nav-anomaly/clickfix calibration items (all not-verified-low-priority) fold into step 0 as "log the value, measure separately, tune if the isolated FP rate exceeds threshold" — do not pre-emptively retune without data.*

## 4. Friend-Advisor Program

From the `ux-gap` findings (ux-advisor and advisor-hunter dominate; capture-pipeline, sw-state, credential-guard, fp-hunter, test-harness corroborate):

**Phase A — Make silent decisions visible (the keystone).** Three independent agents flag that silent allows emit zero events. Add a `nav_silent_allow` EventKind and emit it in the `decision==='allow'` branch (`capture_isolated.ts:1744`) with `score, reasonCodes, nrsFactors, adaptiveAdj, threshold`. Add `cred_form_evaluated` for silently-passed credential forms (advisor-hunter, confirmed). This is the data foundation — without it the journal shows only the loud 5% of decisions and the popup falsely reassures (sw-state *icon badge not persisted* compounds this; confirmed).

**Phase B — Decision Journal UI (priority #4).** Build a unified, reverse-chron timeline merging EventLog + PromptOutcome by domain+time proximity. Per entry: timestamp, source→dest, decision, score vs threshold (base + adaptive = effective), factor breakdown in plain English, user verdict. Recommended home: **Chrome Side Panel** (persistent, non-interruptive — satisfies "advisor" without warning fatigue). Add filtering by kind/domain and CSV/JSON export.

**Phase C — Wire explanations everywhere + verbose mode.** `explainReasonCode` is currently used only in toasts. Wire it into: options event log rows, popup signal chips (as `title`/hover), and the credential modal (which shows raw labels with no point values or remediation). Promote the existing `debug` overlay to a user-readable "verbose mode" per-event card (full CDS/NRS breakdown + "why" + "what would have happened"). Coverage audit: ensure every reason code reachable by a user — including SRI (`SRI_MISSING_ON_CREDENTIAL_PAGE`), `CONTENT_FP`, `nrs_domain_repeat_offender` — has an `explanations.ts` entry (reputation-content *SRI/CSP code names only*, confirmed; ux-advisor *NRS factor mapping gaps*).

**Phase D — Recovery + feedback affordances.** Add "Add to allowlist" / "Undo (<5s)" actions to *block* toasts (prompt toasts already have them; credential paste warnings already have "Trust this site" — verified). Add the mislabel button (shared with priority #8). Add inline help for Smart/Strict/Off mode and trust-button semantics. Leverage the already-robust `ui_toast.ts` multi-action framework (ux-advisor *Toast action framework underutilized*, a confirmed reusable asset).

**Measurement:** add explanation-coverage % and journal-completeness metrics (test-harness *FRIEND-ADVISOR goal unmeasured*).

## 5. Feedback-Capture Program

From the `telemetry-gap` findings (telemetry-feedback, feedback-hunter, scoring-core, capture-pipeline converge):

**Step 1 — Widen the payload (priority #2, the unblocker).** This is the load-bearing change repeated by six agents. Extend `PromptOutcomeEntry` to a replay-grade feature vector and populate it at all verdict sites. Fix the nav-vs-credential inconsistency (nav drops `reasons`; credential keeps it).

**Step 2 — Capture the full distribution.** Record silent allows (shares the `nav_silent_allow` event from §4 Phase A) so adaptive scoring has ground-truth safe-domain signal, not just contested edge cases (feedback-hunter *Silent allows produce zero telemetry*, confirmed; telemetry-feedback *Silent allows don't record outcomes*). Record nav-prompt `ignore`/`timeout` outcomes via `pagehide`/`beforeunload` so abandoned prompts aren't lost (telemetry-feedback *Navigation prompts don't record ignore*, confirmed — root cause is page-unload destroying the toast before `onDismiss`).

**Step 3 — Label the corpus.** Add the `wasWrong`/`label` field + the one-tap mislabel affordance (priority #8). Discount FP-labeled outcomes in `computeAdjustment`. This converts behavior log → supervised training set.

**Step 4 — Storage + export for the flywheel.** Move from the ~500-entry `chrome.storage.local` ring toward IndexedDB + `unlimitedStorage` for an unbounded single-user corpus (privacy-unconstrained locally). The `exportAll()` path exists (verified — the scoring-core "no export" claim was corrected to partially-confirmed; the real gap is *schema richness*, not the export mechanism), so the work is enriching the exported schema, not building export. Add event↔outcome linkage (`eventId` foreign key) and capture adaptive-adjustment state at decision time so outcomes are offline-replayable.

**Step 5 — Close the loop.** Offline: re-tune NRS/CDS weights via logistic regression over feature→verdict pairs; replay the corpus to measure FP/TP delta before shipping any scoring change (this is the principled upgrade to `adaptive_scoring.ts`). Add capture-record-completeness as a measured metric.

*Lower-priority (not-verified) items — per-factor adaptive weights, adjustment-change audit log, stats segmentation, delivery-failure surfacing (#188 residual) — are step-6 refinements once the rich schema lands.*

## 6. Architecture & Platform Program

From the `architecture` findings (architecture-hunter, capture-pipeline, sw-state, reputation-content, scoring-core, credential-guard):

**Posture (sober cost/benefit):**
- **Extension (Chrome MV3): harden in place.** Fix the bridge session-replay/re-pin weakness with SW-vouched init auth (#186 — main-world-guards *Bridge session replay*, confirmed high) and add a ping/pong **post-verification liveness check** to the bridge (architecture-hunter *No liveness check* — verified nuance: the existing ping/pong is one-time at init, not periodic; a dead port after verification silently swallows all signals). Fix the per-frame domain-profile race (#181) by routing `recordNavigation` through the single-threaded SW. Add DNR dynamic rules fed by the bloom list to *hard-block* known-bad domains (the only MV3-native way to prevent, not just react).
- **Firefox build: the biggest unrealized lever.** FF-01 + `manifest.firefox.json` are merged but unwired. **AI-4 (OPEN)** must be decided first. Firefox's retained blocking `webRequest` enables true pre-commit blocking and HTTP-header CSP inspection (closes #179 structurally on FF). Also fixes FF-03 (session fallback not auto-cleared on restart — sw-state/architecture-hunter, confirmed; note the deeper verified bug: `session_state.ts:191` hardcodes `chrome.storage.session` and never uses the `storageSessionShim`, so FF would crash on hydrate — fix this *before* FF-03). Recommendation per the verified trade-off analysis: `web-ext` (option b) for a solo dev — battle-tested, decoupled, fewer surprises.
- **Native-messaging companion: highest ceiling, design now (priority #10).** Unlocks DNS inspection, persistent state (no SW death), heavy ML inference, CSP-header capture, download scanning, subframe/cross-origin validation — structurally fixing the cluster of MV3 limits (CSP blindness #179, bloom staleness, cross-origin iframe blindness, subframe XSS). For a single-user dev machine the native-host install friction is acceptable.
- **Browser fork: recommend AGAINST.** Chromium-rebase treadmill is a full-time team's job; extension + native-companion + Firefox-blocking delivers ~all the security value at a fraction of the cost.

**Visual-sim decision (blocks on AI-5, OPEN).** Pipeline is plumbing-complete but inert (placeholder hashes — confirmed; the hashes are deterministic SHA-256 of brand IDs, *not* seeded PRNG as some descriptions said, and thresholds make accidental matches statistically impossible). The verified architectural limit: aHash/bHash perceptual hashing is evadable (visual-js-p4, partially-confirmed — note the design doc deliberately chose this over color-sensitive dHash). Recommendation: keep pHash as a cheap pre-filter only; pivot the confirmation stage to logo CNN/Siamese embeddings or an on-device VLM (Gemini Nano multimodal via offscreen document). This may moot AI-5's need for screenshot-derived perceptual templates.

**Surviving high/critical architecture findings explicitly accounted for:** bloom staleness (§2 #6, §6 DNR/companion), CSP header blindness (§6 Firefox/companion), iframe/subframe inspection (§6 companion), domain-profile race #181 (§6 harden), bridge replay #186 + liveness (§6 harden), Firefox port + FF-03 (§6 Firefox), pre-commit blocking (§6 DNR + Firefox), visual-sim inert (§6 visual-sim decision), icon-badge not persisted (§4 Phase A — persist to `SessionStateManager`).

## 8. Existing Assets to Leverage

Strong, verified, reusable foundations — extend these, don't rebuild:

**Scoring & detection (mature, well-tested):**
- `scoring.ts` CDS model — modular, compositional, comprehensive reason codes, clean `ClickContext → ScoreResult` API.
- `nrs.ts` — composable multi-detector integration (10+ factors, explicit weights, diminishing returns, proper gating of CSP/nav-anomaly above base-NRS-20 — the gating is load-bearing for FP avoidance and was the verified mitigation several FP claims missed).
- `domain_groups.ts` — explicit, auditable same-org suppression (already fixed unity3d.com).
- `domain.ts` — PSL trie registrable-domain parsing, lookalike detection, brand aliases.
- `domain_profile.ts` — per-domain history with 30-day decay + LRU; the substrate for familiarity/trust-tier suppression.
- `adaptive_scoring.ts` — principled per-domain adjustment with min-outcomes gate (just needs to be *applied* and *fed richer data*).
- `password_field.ts` (#196) — robust shared honeypot-resistant credential-field detector; the canonical gate for any new credential signal.
- `redirect_chain.ts`, `nav_anomaly.ts`, `reputation.ts` bloom (mathematically sound) — solid detectors.

**Infrastructure (production-grade):**
- `session_state.ts` `SessionStateManager` — write-through cache, atomic hydrate, defensive validation; survives SW restarts. Add the icon-badge and decision-journal keys here.
- `storage.ts` — append/serialize/retry/reset-barrier, `exportAll()`, bounded logs. The capture-enrichment work rides on this, not a rewrite.
- `browser.ts` — complete `browser.*` compat shim (FF-01 merged); the Firefox on-ramp (fix the hydrate hardcoding noted in §6 first).
- `bridge_outbound.ts` — priority-buffered outbound queue; attack-onset signals never dropped pre-verification.
- `main_guard.ts` — challenge-response handshake + proactive JS-API patching (the *primary* defense, per the verified correction — not mere rollback).

**UX & explainability (building blocks present, underused):**
- `explanations.ts` — 41–49 reason codes → plain English; the friend-advisor dictionary (wire it into all surfaces).
- `debug_overlay.ts` — already renders the full decision context; repurpose its layout for the user-facing journal/verbose card.
- `ui_toast.ts` — Shadow-DOM-isolated, multi-action, accessible toast framework (underutilized — extend for recovery actions).
- `credential_modal.ts` — fully accessible (ARIA, focus trap, keyboard); add the score breakdown + remediation.
- `popup_model.ts` — reusable, tested decision-logic functions; extend for journal/explanation surfacing.
- `event_tone.ts` — event categorization for UI theming.

**Verification (exists, needs CI-gating):**
- `measure-fp.mjs` (Tranco methodology, phase separation), `benchmark.mjs` (53 gym fixtures, 7 categories, per-category thresholds), corpus validation infra. The gap is *continuous CI gating* and *deeper flow coverage*, not absent tooling (test-harness, confirmed). Wire these into a blocking Smart-Mode-Silence gate (§3 step 0).
